# Local patches to vendored playsrc crates

Upstream: `Hona/playsrc` @ `12f36e63`. Every patched site has a `bunnyhop patch:` comment.

## movement (`playsrc-movement`)

| Change | Where | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `Policy::clamp_ground_speed` (default `true`) gates the post-`Accelerate` horizontal speed clamp in the walk branch. | `lib.rs` `Policy`, `movement.rs` `full_walk` | TF2's `WalkMove` clamps ground speed to maxspeed. SDK 2013 `CGameMovement::WalkMove` (and CS:S) does not; there, only friction slows a fast landing. bunnyhop sets `false`. |
| `Policy::crouch_command_crop: CrouchCommandCrop` (default `GroundedCrouched`). `AnyDuckState` crops forward/side/up by `crouched_command_factor` when duck is held, ducking, or ducked, on the ground **and in the air**. It is evaluated against the duck state *before* this tick's duck update. | `lib.rs`, `movement.rs` `step` / `crop_crouched_command` | SDK `HandleDuckingSpeedCrop` only crops when `FL_DUCKING` and on the ground. CS:S crops on any duck state (0.34). bunnyhop uses `AnyDuckState`. |
| `Policy::air_crouch_lift: Option<f32>` (default `None` = full hull height difference). This is the origin offset used by an airborne duck, an airborne unduck, and the airborne `can_unduck` probe. | `lib.rs`, `movement.rs` `update_crouch` / `can_unduck` / `air_crouch_delta` | SDK `FinishDuck` lifts the origin by the full standing-crouched delta (17 units for CS:S hulls). CS:S shrinks the hull around its centre (half: 8.5), which gives the documented ~65-unit crouch-jump instead of ~72. bunnyhop uses `Some(8.5)`. |
| With `replace_vertical_while_ducking`, the jump impulse replaces vz while ducking **or fully ducked**. Previously this only happened mid-transition. | `movement.rs` `check_jump` | SDK `CheckJumpButton`: `if (m_bDucking \|\| FL_DUCKING) vz = impulse; else vz += impulse`. |
| `simple_spline` result clamped to `[0, 1]`. | `movement.rs` | f32 rounding gave `1.0000001` one tick before a 0.4 s duck finished at 100 tick. `validate_output` then rejected the state, so every ground duck errored the step. |
| Test helper `tf2_policy()` uses `..Policy::default()` for the new fields. | `tests.rs` | Keeps upstream tests compiling. All 30 upstream tests still pass. |
| `Tracer::ground_surface(&Trace) -> Option<SurfaceProperties>` (default `None`). New `GroundState::jump_factor`. CategorizePosition sets `surface_friction = min(friction·1.25, 1)` from it, and CheckJumpButton multiplies the impulse by the ground's jump factor. | `lib.rs`, `movement.rs` `categorize_position` / `check_jump` | SDK `CategorizeGroundSurface` and `flGroundFactor`. The port only had static policy values. |
| `Configuration::fixes: MovementFixes { downhill, uphill, rampbug }`, all `false` by default. | `lib.rs`, `movement.rs` `full_walk` / `slide` / `unstick` | Optional timer-plugin fixes (slopefix/RNGFix downhill, RNGFix uphill, rampbug). See MOVEMENT_AUDIT.md §9. Vanilla when off. Downhill covers initial/crouch ground probes as well as post-move probes, excludes rising/swimming players, and does not double-clip collision landings. |
| `MovementFixes::rngfix_incline` / `rngfix_edge` (default `false`), `StepResult::air_move_velocity` / `move_collided` / `prevented_collision`, `PreventedCollision`. Before an airborne TryPlayerMove, the first trace of the move decides RNGFix's uphill / edge-bug `PreventCollision` (the move starts at `collision point - velocity * tick + 0.1 up`, skipped if that start is solid); with `rngfix_incline`, `fix_downhill_landing_rngfix` replaces `fix_downhill_landing` (base velocity included, nothing after a move that hit something, downhill always / uphill only when faster). | `lib.rs`, `movement.rs` `full_walk` / `rngfix_prevent_collision` / `fix_downhill_landing_rngfix` / `fix_early_downhill_landing` | jason-e/rngfix 1.1.3 parity (physics v17, research/RNGFIX-1025.md). The plugin predicts the move before ProcessMovement; here the real move's values are used. Off: unchanged. |
| `Configuration::record_queries` (default `true`). When `false`, `QueryContext` does not record traces into `StepResult::queries` / `point_queries`. | `lib.rs`, `movement.rs` | One allocation per trace, used only for diagnostics. bunnyhop turns it off. |
| `Policy::unduck_checks_destination` (default `false`). `can_unduck` also does a stationary standing-hull test at the destination. | `lib.rs`, `movement.rs` `can_unduck` | Swept traces against displacements never report start-solid, so an airborne unduck could end inside a steep displacement wall, deeper than CheckStuck's nudges reach (permanent stuck, found by the fuzzer on arcane). bunnyhop sets `true`. |
| `CrouchState::uses_crouched_hull`: Unducking counts as crouched only if it started fully ducked (`start_fraction >= 1`). Unducking + duck pressed again from a full duck returns to `Crouched` at once instead of entering `Ducking`. | `lib.rs`, `movement.rs` `update_crouch` | SDK hulls follow FL_DUCKING (set by FinishDuck). Before: (a) releasing duck mid-transition switched to the crouched hull for a tick, so the player slid under an overhang and then stood up inside it; (b) re-ducking while unducking switched to the standing hull with no CanUnduck. Both are permanent stuck cases found by the fuzzer. |
| `validate_output` no longer bounds the base velocity by `maximum_velocity` (sv_maxvelocity). | `movement.rs` `validate_output` | Source's CheckVelocity clamps only the velocity; a trigger_push faster than 3500 u/s (bhop_exceptional's 10000 u/s booster) made every step fail. |
| `Configuration::gravity_scale` may be negative (validated as finite only). | `movement.rs` `validate_configuration` | CBaseEntity's "gravity" keyvalue is a plain atof and StartGravity / FinishGravity use it as is, so a negative value accelerates the player upward. bhop_alt_saimaa's jump pad (`AddOutput gravity -0.5`) relies on it; bit-exact with the real engine (tools/parity). |
| `Policy::jump_while_unducking` and `Policy::air_unduck_from_transition` (both default `false`). The first lets `check_jump` jump in the `Unducking` phase (and the jump then replaces vz, as while ducking); the second runs FinishUnDuck when duck is released in the air from a partial duck/unduck transition (origin drops by the air crouch delta once `can_unduck` finds room). | `lib.rs`, `movement.rs` `check_jump` / `update_crouch` | SDK `CheckJumpButton` refuses while `m_bDucking && FL_DUCKING`; CS:S jumps, so ducking in the air and releasing as you land keeps the hop (tools/parity crouch-hops). bunnyhop sets both only for physics v2 (game.rs `PHYSICS_V2`); v1 keeps the SDK rule. |
| A start-solid water-exit waist trace uses a zero plane instead of failing (`water-waist-plane`). A ladder trace without a plane is "no ladder" instead of failing (`ladder-plane`). | `movement.rs` `check_water_exit` / `update_ladder` | These returned `Err`, which wedged the browser client (bhop_cartoons). SDK 2013 uses the zero plane normal. |

## collision (`playsrc-collision`)

| Change | Where | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Brush hits set `Trace::surface = SurfaceIdentity { registry: TEXINFO_SURFACE_REGISTRY, index: texinfo }` (cleared on all-solid). | `lib.rs` `trace_brushes` | Callers can resolve the hit material's surface properties. Displacement hits already carried a `SurfaceIdentity`; bunnyhop supplies those with its own registry tag. |
| Zero-area displacement triangles (`degenerate-displacement-triangles`). A triangle whose normal can't be normalized (coincident grid vertices) gets a zero normal and distance instead of failing the build with `InvalidRange`. Box sweeps skip its face plane, so it collides as a segment through its axis and edge planes. Rays can't hit it, and stationary boxes use the usual overlap test. New `World::degenerate_displacement_triangles()` lists `(source, count)`; `crates/core` reports these as physics diagnostics. Test: `zero_area_displacement_triangles_collide_as_segments`. | `displacement.rs` `build` / `sweep_box_triangle` / `ray_triangle`, `lib.rs` | bhop_exodus (displacements 174/175: 62 triangles), bhop_bitches_fix (2–5: 92) and bhop_boxes_snowy (26: 97) have sewn or collapsed displacement rows, and the whole map failed to load (`displacements: InvalidRange`). SDK 2013 `CDispCollTri::CalcPlane` keeps these triangles, because `VectorNormalize` maps a zero vector to zero. Its zero face plane then "enters" at fraction 0 with a zero impact normal whenever no other plane entered later. The movement code rejects that as a malformed trace, and on exodus it does happen. Skipping only that plane keeps the exact box-vs-segment test. Triangle indices are unchanged. Maps without such triangles are unaffected: the change only applies when `normal == [0; 3]`, which used to be a load error. |
| `World::trace_brush_model_vphysics(model, request, inset, separate)`: with `separate`, a box trace against an inset (VPhysics) brush that starts outside a face and doesn't move toward it (`delta` along that axis ≤ 0 / ≥ 0; general brushes: `d1 > 0 && d2 >= d1`) never hits that brush, even inside the DIST_EPSILON reach. `trace_brush_model_inset` is unchanged (`separate = false`). | `lib.rs` `trace_model_hull_inset` / `trace_headnode` / `trace_brushes` / `clip_box_brush` | Landing on a func_door could leave the feet 1–2 ulps inside the 1/32 band; the rest of the move (or a stationary stuck test) then "entered" the brush at fraction 0 through an unrelated face (the bottom, or -y) and the movement code zeroed the velocity (bhop_redwood; 17 of 444 prod replays hit it). The real CS:S engine keeps moving, bit-exact with `separate` (tools/parity). bunnyhop enables it from physics v3. |

## bsp (`playsrc-bsp`)

| Change | Where | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `Profile::Source2013V20` now accepts container version 19 as well as 20 (`Profile::accepts`). The version 19 rejection test became an acceptance test, plus rejection tests for 18 and 21. | `lib.rs` | The Source 2013 engine loads BSP v19 (MINBSPVERSION) and v20. The lumps this crate decodes have the same layouts in v19. LZMA is never used in v19, and the older leaf/static-prop lump versions are already selected per lump version. |
| Static prop game lump versions 4 (56-byte records) and 5 (60-byte records) are accepted, alongside 6 and 10. Fields that are missing in older versions default to forced fade scale 1 and DX levels 0. | `game_lump.rs` | CS:S-era maps use v4/v5. Before, any such map's static props failed to parse. |
| An unreadable pakfile lump no longer fails the parse: `lump.pak` becomes `None`, and the raw bytes are still available. | `lib.rs` | bhop_lego and bhop_null have zips the strict validator rejects (`InvalidPak`). bunnyhop reads the pak through its own lenient zip index. |
| New `Profile::CsgoV21` (accepts only container version 21) and `Profile::for_source(bytes)`, which picks it for v21 headers and `Source2013V20` otherwise. `Source2013V20` still rejects 21. Tests: `csgo_profile_accepts_only_v21_and_is_selected_from_the_header`. | `lib.rs` | CS:GO maps (research/CSGO-MAPS.md). The lumps this crate decodes have the same layouts in v21 (faces v1, leaves v1, 176-byte displacement info, 8-byte brush sides), checked on 34 CS:GO bhop maps. v19/v20 parsing is unchanged. |
| Under `CsgoV21`, the lighting lumps (8, 53) stay raw (`LumpData::Opaque`; `Lump::bytes`), and `csgo_light_samples(bytes, offset, count)` reads a face's RGBE samples at its byte offset. Test: `csgo_lighting_stays_raw_and_reads_unaligned_face_samples`. | `lib.rs` | CS:GO's VRAD stores one more byte per luxel after each face's samples, so face light offsets and the lump length aren't multiples of 4 (7 of the 33 maps checked failed with `InvalidRecord`, and the others would have read shifted samples). |
| Static props under `CsgoV21`: `sprp` v10 is CS:GO's 76-byte record, v11 the 80-byte one with a uniform scale, v9 the 72-byte one. The 8-bit flags are promoted like the CS:S-era versions; DX levels are 0 (CS:GO stores CPU/GPU levels there). New occurrence fields `uniform_scale` (1.0 unless v11) and `diffuse_modulation` (`None` before v9). Tests: `decodes_csgo_v10_and_v11_records_under_the_csgo_profile`, `csgo_and_source_2013_v10_layouts_stay_profile_selected`. | `game_lump.rs` | The Source 2013 v10 record is 72 bytes; CS:GO's v10 is a different layout with the same version number, so the profile selects it. |

## vpk (`playsrc-vpk`)

Vendored from `packages/formats/vpk/rust` at the same commit.

| Change | Where | Why |
|---|---|---|
| The default feature set is empty: `signature-verification` (rsa + sha2) is opt-in. | `Cargo.toml` | Nothing here verifies Valve's VPK signatures, and the RSA stack would bloat the WASM build. Parsing, CRC32 checks on reads and archive MD5 records are unchanged; only `verify_self`/`verify_signature` need the feature. Upstream tests need it: `cargo test -p playsrc-vpk --features signature-verification` (4 pass). |

`crates/core` reads only the `_dir.vpk` tree. Archive chunks (`_NNN.vpk`) are read lazily by `(archive index, offset,
length)` through `SegmentReader` (`crates/core/src/vfs.rs`, `VpkMount::assemble`), so multi-GB archives are never
loaded whole.

The studio-model crate is not vendored. Static props use a small LOD-0 MDL/VVD/VTX reader in
`crates/core/src/props.rs` instead, because upstream's crate (about 14k lines, plus `playsrc-vhv`) covers animation,
flexes and eyes, none of which static props need.

Animated player models still don't vendor it. `crates/core/src/studio.rs` extends that reader with what the CS:S
player models need: bones (quaternion-interp `$proceduralbones` data is parsed; the CS:S player models have none), skinned LOD-0 geometry (VVD bone weights,
tangents), attachments, pose parameters, sequences with blend grids, `$weightlist`s and autolayers, `$includemodel`
merging (the engine's virtual model: bones, sequences and pose parameters matched by name) and the compressed
animation decoder (`mstudioanim_t` chains, RLE euler values, Quaternion48/64, Vector48). The decoder follows the
public SDK 2013 `bone_setup.cpp`, cross-checked against upstream's `decode_frame`. Upstream's crate would add ~14k
lines plus `playsrc-vhv` to the WASM for flexes, eyes, IK and presentation code that the player models don't use, and
it would still need a bridge to the client's bone setup (`apps/web/src/player/studio/pose.ts`).

### Optional crouch support recategorization (physics v11)

`Policy::recategorize_after_crouch` defaults off. When enabled, a completed crouch/uncrouch hull or origin change recategorizes ground support before jump/movement, matching Source `FinishDuck`/`FinishUnDuck`. The synthetic-floor regression covers an air-unduck entering the two-unit ground probe and jumping on the same command; disabled behavior remains unchanged. This does not change the game's historical airborne autohop input stripping or enable server plugins.
